subject: literature
passage: Ewa had taught her little cousin Piotr to swim, so she expected to teach him to ski as well. On the first morning, though, she fell three times before the slope even began. Piotr, who had skied since he was four, glided back to her, showed her how to angle her skis into a wedge, and waited while she tried again. By afternoon Ewa was sliding slowly down the gentle slope, with Piotr calling out instructions behind her.
stem: Which choice best states the main idea of the text?

choices.A: Piotr learned to ski at a young age because Ewa taught him.
choices.B: Ewa, used to teaching her cousin, finds herself being taught by him instead.
choices.C: Ewa decides that skiing is too difficult for her to learn in a single day.
choices.D: Piotr refuses to help Ewa because she has always treated him like a small child.

explanation.why: The first sentence sets up Ewa's expectation: she has always been the teacher, so she "expected to teach him to ski as well." The rest of the text reverses this: Piotr shows her how to ski and calls out instructions. The main idea is this switch in roles.
explanation.A: Incorrect. The text says Piotr has skied since he was four but never says who taught him; Ewa is the one learning to ski.
explanation.B: Correct. This covers the setup (Ewa as the usual teacher) and the turn (Piotr teaching her).
explanation.C: Incorrect. By afternoon Ewa is sliding down the slope with Piotr's help, so she does not give up.
explanation.D: Incorrect. Piotr helps Ewa right away, gliding back to her and showing her what to do.
